title: Account Administrator
description:
We are proud to be recruiting on behalf of a thriving, growing, and dynamic organisation that is looking for a talented and motivated Account Administrator to join their team. This is a company that is genuinely going places - and they want the right person to grow with them.

If you are someone who takes pride in keeping things running smoothly, enjoys being the backbone of a busy team, and thrives in a fast-paced environment, this could be the perfect next step in your career.

What You Will Be Doing
- Providing comprehensive administrative support across the business
- Managing diaries, scheduling meetings, and coordinating appointments
- Handling correspondence - emails, letters, and phone calls - in a professional and timely manner
- Maintaining accurate records, filing systems, and databases
- Preparing documents, reports, and presentations as required
- Supporting various departments with day-to-day administrative tasks
- Acting as a first point of contact for internal and external queries

What We Are Looking For
- Previous experience in an administrative or office support role
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities
- Strong written and verbal communication skills
- Proficient in Microsoft Office - Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint
- A positive, can-do attitude with a high level of attention to detail
- Ability to work both independently and as part of a team
- Discretion and professionalism when handling confidential information

What Is On Offer
- A role within a genuinely thriving and ambitious organisation with real momentum
- Fantastic opportunities to develop your career and take on greater responsibility as the business grows
- Supportive, energetic team culture where hard work is recognised and rewarded
- 28 days annual leave including bank holidays

This role is exclusively available through Consula.

To be considered, you must apply via Consula. Applications submitted through any other channel will not be accepted.

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
We are currently recruiting for an Accounts Payable / Accounts Receivable Clerk to join an established finance team on a temporary-to-permanent basis.

This is a great opportunity for an experienced candidate looking to develop their career within the automotive/manufacturing sector, with the potential to secure a permanent position following a successful temporary period.

The ideal candidate will have previous experience across Purchase Ledger and/or Sales Ledger, with a good understanding of invoice processing, reconciliations and general finance administration.

Experience within the automotive or manufacturing sector would be highly desirable. Candidates with previous experience of self-billing invoices will also be strongly considered.

Key Responsibilities
Processing purchase invoices and maintaining the Purchase Ledger
Processing sales invoices and maintaining the Sales Ledger
Matching invoices against purchase orders and supporting documentation
Processing and managing self-billing invoices
Completing supplier and customer account reconciliations
Investigating and resolving invoice and payment discrepancies
Supporting payment runs and ensuring invoices are processed accurately and on time
Responding to queries from suppliers, customers and internal departments
Maintaining accurate financial records and ensuring information is kept up to date
Providing general support to the wider finance team as required
About You

We are looking for someone who:

Has previous experience in Purchase Ledger, Sales Ledger, Accounts Payable and/or Accounts Receivable
Has good attention to detail and takes pride in maintaining accurate records
Is confident dealing with suppliers, customers and internal stakeholders
Has experience processing high volumes of invoices
Has a good understanding of reconciliations and resolving discrepancies
Is organised and able to manage their workload effectively
Has strong Excel and general IT skills
Automotive/manufacturing experience would be advantageous
Experience with self-billing invoices would be beneficial
The Opportunity

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who is looking for a temporary position with a genuine opportunity to become permanent. The successful candidate will join a small, busy finance team and gain valuable experience within an established automotive/manufacturing business in Bartley Green
This is office working and hours are 8.30am-4.30pm with a finish at 3.30pm on a Friday

title: Bookkeeper
description:
Bookkeeper

Birmingham Hybrid Working £30,000 - £35,000 Permanent

Key Responsibilities
- Maintaining accurate financial records and bookkeeping processes
- Managing accounts payable and ensuring suppliers are paid promptly
- Overseeing sales ledger activities and customer account balances
- Completing bank and balance sheet reconciliations
- Processing employee expenses and company card transactions
- Preparing and submitting VAT returns
- Assisting with month-end close activities
- Posting journals and maintaining accounting records
- Monitoring cash flow and supporting financial planning
- Liaising with suppliers, customers, and internal teams regarding finance queries
- Supporting improvements to financial controls and processes

About You

To be successful in this role, you'll bring previous bookkeeping experience and a hands-on approach to finance.

You'll have:
- Experience working in a Bookkeeper or similar accounts position
- Strong knowledge of double-entry bookkeeping principles
- Confidence managing both purchase and sales ledgers
- Experience completing bank reconciliations and VAT returns
- Strong working knowledge of accounting packages such as Xero, Sage or QuickBooks
- Good Excel skills and a high level of accuracy
- Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail
- The ability to manage deadlines and prioritise workloads effectively

Additional Experience That Would Be Beneficial
- AAT qualified or studying towards an accounting qualification
- Previous experience within an SME environment
- Exposure to month-end accounting procedures

What's on Offer
- A broad and varied bookkeeping role with genuine responsibility
- The opportunity to join a business during an exciting period of growth
- A supportive and collaborative working environment
- Hybrid working arrangements
- Ongoing development opportunities
- The chance to make a visible impact within the finance function

At Gleeson Recruitment Group, we embrace inclusivity and welcome applicants of all backgrounds, experiences, and abilities. We are proud to be a disability confident employer.

By applying you will be registered as a candidate with Gleeson Recruitment Limited. Our Privacy Policy is available on our website and explains how we will use your data.

title: Credit Control
description:
A leading organisation is looking to recruit an experienced Credit Controller, from a legal backgorund, to join its finance team. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys taking ownership, working through the detail and ensuring matters are followed through to completion. If you are confident managing the full credit control process, enjoy developing strong relationships with clients and fee earners and have a commercially focused approach to achieving results, this could be an ideal next step. Based in Birmingham with hybrid working available, you'll be joining a well-established and supportive organisation where your knowledge, experience and ideas will make a real difference.

Working as part of a collaborative finance team, you will take responsibility for the end-to-end credit control function, proactively managing client accounts and driving prompt cash collection. You will develop strong relationships with clients, fee earners and senior internal stakeholders, take ownership of aged debt, identify and overcome payment obstacles, resolve invoice queries and disputes, allocate cash and reconcile accounts. You will also support regular cash collection and aged debt reviews, provide useful management information, assess credit risk and confidently escalate complex or higher-risk debt to senior business leaders and the Finance Director where appropriate. The role will also give you the opportunity to identify and introduce improvements across credit control processes, systems and ways of working.

Ideally you will have:
- Previous experience within Credit Control or Accounts Receivable, preferably gained within a legal, professional services or partnership environment.
- Strong experience managing end-to-end credit control activities, including aged debt, cash collection, credit risk, account reconciliations and resolving payment disputes.
- Excellent communication and relationship management skills, with the confidence to challenge, influence and build effective relationships with senior stakeholders, fee earners and client contacts.
- Strong organisational and analytical abilities, with advanced Excel skills and experience working with finance or practice management systems such as Aderant, Elite 3 E, Microsoft Dynamics 365 or similar.

In return, you will receive:
- The opportunity to join a respected organisation and take ownership of a key Credit Control Specialist position within the finance team.
- Hybrid and flexible working options, together with competitive holiday entitlement and family-friendly policies designed to support a positive work-life balance.
- A supportive, collaborative and inclusive working environment where your expertise, ideas and contribution are recognised, alongside continued learning and development opportunities.
- A comprehensive benefits package including private healthcare, well-being initiatives, mentoring opportunities, professional development and support with professional memberships.

If you are an experienced Credit Controller within the legal sector who enjoys taking responsibility, managing the complete credit control process and achieving positive commercial outcomes, we'd love to hear from you. Apply now!

title: Finance Administrator
description:
An established and growing organisation within the property sector is seeking a motivated Finance Administrator to join its finance team. This is an excellent opportunity for a professional and organised individual looking to gain valuable experience within a supportive and collaborative environment. The role would suit someone with previous finance or administration experience, as well as a strong junior candidate looking to gain practical experience within a finance environment. Working alongside experienced finance colleagues, you will receive support and training while gaining exposure to a broad range of financial and administrative duties.

As a Finance Administrator, you will support the day-to-day financial operations of the business, with a particular focus on invoicing, customer accounts, payments, and general finance administration. You will be responsible for processing invoices, allocating payments, maintaining accurate financial records, assisting with account queries, and supporting the wider finance team with day-to-day tasks. As the role involves regular communication with clients, suppliers, and internal teams, you will need to be confident, professional, and well presented, with excellent communication skills and a strong customer-focused approach.

Ideally you will:
- Have previous experience within finance, accounts, administration, or a customer-focused environment, although a strong junior candidate looking to gain finance experience will also be considered.
- Be professional, confident, and well presented, with excellent communication skills and the ability to build positive relationships with clients, suppliers, and colleagues.
- Demonstrate strong organisational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple tasks accurately within a busy environment.
- Have a positive attitude, willingness to learn, and a genuine interest in gaining practical experience within a finance environment.

In return, you will benefit from:
- Joining a well-established organisation within the property sector with a strong reputation and continued growth plans.
- Working within a supportive finance team where you will receive training, guidance, and the opportunity to develop your skills.
- Gaining valuable practical experience across finance administration, invoicing, customer accounts, payments, and wider financial processes.
- Hybrid flexibility and a positive, professional working environment where you can build your knowledge and experience.

If you are a professional and personable individual looking to gain valuable experience within finance, we would love to hear from you.

title: French or Spanish Speaking Credit Controller
description:
Credit Controller - FTC until May 2027

£30,000 + 10% completion bonus

100% home based

A rapidly expanding international debt collection agency is currently looking for an experienced commercial credit professional with fluent language skills in either French or Spanish, as well as fluency in English, to join its credit management team to work on a high value and complex project until May 2027.

You will be part of a highly experienced and skilled global collections team, where you will be responsible for your own portfolio of customers covering French/Spanish and English speaking markets. You will be actively managing your ledger of c.200 accounts across a range of different industries focusing on maximising cash collection, query management, and working towards targets. Prior experience of working with Oracle is also highly advantageous.

This role will be a home based position.

Duties:
- Optimise cash collection in your ledger for debtors based in French or Spanish speaking markets
- Chasing high value and complex old debt (150+ days)
- Managing complex queries and disputes through to resolution
- Ensuring all updates are logged in a timely manner on system
- Escalation of cases to DCA when appropriate
- Working towards and achieving targets set
- Adhering to country specific legal and financial regulations
- Proactively alert management to any potential compliance issues.

Skills Required:
- Proven experience within commercial debt collection/credit control is essential.
- Fluency in French or Spanish (as well as English) is essential.
- Working knowledge of Oracle is highly advantageous
- Strong negotiation and dispute resolution skills
- Proven ability to work in a target driven environment
- Excellent time management skills
- Outstanding communications skills both verbally and written
- Team player, whilst demonstrating ability to work autonomously (especially as this is a remote based role)
- Excellent customer service skills
- Self motivated, with the ability to multitask and prioritise
- Strong Excel skills

If you are interested in this vacancy please contact CWC Recruitment Ltd. CWC is a specialist recruitment consultancy dedicated to recruiting credit professionals. We have over 45 years of credit control and credit management recruitment experience. We are true experts within our field.

title: International Accounts Officer
description:
International Accounts Officer - Interim

Location: Birmingham - Hybrid (2-3 days per week in the office)
Rate: £19-£23 per hour Umbrella
Contract: 3-6 months
Start: ASAP

We are currently recruiting for an International Accounts Officer to join a busy finance function on an urgent interim basis.

This is a key role within an international finance environment, supporting the accurate and timely processing of financial transactions, donor invoicing and reporting across multiple regions. The successful candidate will play an important part in ensuring international programmes continue to operate smoothly and financial requirements are met.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage donor contract invoicing and ensure compliance with funding requirements across multiple regions.
- Support international project accounting and institutional funding compliance.
- Produce accurate weekly, monthly and quarterly financial reports.
- Support the timely transfer of funds to international and regional offices.
- Monitor financial information and investigate variances or discrepancies.
- Work closely with internal stakeholders and international teams to resolve finance queries.
- Maintain accurate financial records and ensure processes comply with relevant policies and procedures.
- Use financial systems to manage and report on complex international finance activity.

About You

We are looking for an experienced finance professional with a strong understanding of international finance and donor-funded programmes.

You will ideally have:
- A recognised accounting qualification such as ACCA, CIMA or AAT.
- Experience of donor contract invoicing and funding compliance.
- Experience in international project accounting or a similar multi-region finance environment.
- Strong financial reporting experience, including weekly, monthly and quarterly reporting.
- Experience using Unit 4 ERP or a similar complex financial system.
- Excellent attention to detail and the ability to work accurately under pressure.
- Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to build effective relationships across different teams and locations.
- The ability to quickly understand complex financial requirements and work independently.

Why Apply?

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced finance professional to take on an immediate interim assignment within a complex international finance environment, working closely with a range of stakeholders and supporting programmes across multiple regions.

Please note: This is a hybrid role requiring 2-3 days per week in the Birmingham office.

If you are available at short notice and have the international finance and donor funding experience required, we would be keen to hear from you.

title: Payroll Assistant
description:
Totum Partners is partnering with a leading law firm to recruit a Payroll Assistant on a 6-month fixed-term contract. Based in Birmingham and working four days per week, this role will support the accurate and timely delivery of the monthly payroll, including payroll changes, benefits and pension updates, statutory payments and payroll reporting. Experience using ADP/NGUX is essential.

The ideal Payroll Assistant will be responsible for:
- Processing starters and leavers on ADP/NGUX.
- Resolving employee payroll queries, including tax issues and system login problems.
- Managing monthly payroll changes and ad hoc reports.
- Managing overtime forms and reconciling against payroll outputs.
- Calculating and processing sickness payments.
- Administering statutory parental leave payments.
- Processing pension and benefits variations.
- Raising and processing ad hoc employee payments.
- Checking and issuing HMRC/PAYE payments.
- Delivering end-of-month reporting.
- Supporting the payroll team with ad hoc tasks.

The ideal Payroll Assistant will be responsible for:
- Previous payroll administration experience, preferably within professional services.
- Proven experience using ADP/NGUX payroll software.
- Understanding of manual Tax and NI calculations.
- Up-to-date knowledge of HMRC statutory regulations.
- Good Microsoft Excel skills.
- High levels of discretion and integrity.
- Strong attention to detail.
- Excellent time management skills and the ability to work to deadlines.
- CIPP qualification desirable but not essential.

Equal Opportunities

As a responsible business, it is important that we represent the diversity of our people, our clients and our communities. We believe that the firms that thrive are those with the most diverse team; that's why we work so hard to source the best talent from the broadest pool possible. As an equal opportunities employer we strive to accommodate anyone who may have specific needs. If you require reasonable adjustments to be made during the selection process, please talk to a member of the recruitment team so that any required adjustments can be made in advance.

title: Accounts Administrator & Cashier
description:
A national and well-established solicitors firm is seeking a motivated Accounts Administrator & Cashier to join its Finance team. This is an excellent opportunity for a professional and organised individual looking to develop valuable experience within a supportive and collaborative environment. The role would suit someone with previous finance, accounts, or administration experience, as well as a strong junior candidate looking to gain practical experience within a professional finance environment. Full training will be provided while gaining exposure to a broad range of client account, cashiering, and financial administration duties.

As an Accounts Administrator & Cashier, you will support the day-to-day running of client accounts, with a particular focus on payments, reconciliations, compliance, and general finance administration. You will be responsible for checking completion statements, posting bills, posting monies received from clients, completing bank reconciliations, transferring monies between accounts, checking ledger statements, and completing compliance, money laundering, and fraud checks. As the role involves regular communication with solicitors and internal departments, you will need to be confident, professional, and well organised, with excellent communication skills and a strong attention to detail.

Ideally you will:
- Have previous experience within finance, accounts, administration, or a similar environment, although a strong junior candidate looking to gain finance experience will also be considered.
- Be highly numerate and accurate, with excellent attention to detail and the ability to maintain accurate financial records and processes.
- Demonstrate strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage your own workload, work well under pressure, and meet tight deadlines.
- Have excellent communication skills, with the ability to liaise effectively with solicitors, internal departments, and colleagues across the business.

In return, you will benefit from:
- Joining a well-established national solicitors firm with a strong reputation and working as part of a professional Finance team.
- Working within a supportive finance team where you will receive full training, guidance, and the opportunity to develop your skills.
- Gaining valuable practical experience across client accounts, cashiering, bank reconciliations, payments, compliance checks, and wider financial processes.
- A permanent, full-time position offering hybrid flexibility to give a great work-life balance.

If you are a professional, highly numerate, and organised individual looking to develop valuable experience within a professional Finance team, we would love to hear from you.

title: Accounts Payable Administrator
description:
Accounts Payable Administrator
Location: Solihull, West Midlands, B91 2 AA
Hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00am - 5:00pm
Pay Rate: £13.85 - £14.36 per hour
Contract: Full-Time, Temporary (3 Months)

We're looking for an Accounts Payable Administrator to join our busy Shared Services Finance team in Solihull on a temporary basis.
This is an excellent opportunity to gain valuable experience within a leading FMCG business, supporting a high-performing Accounts Payable function. You'll play a key role in ensuring supplier invoices are processed accurately, queries are resolved efficiently, and financial controls are maintained to the highest standards.

What You'll Be Doing
Invoice Processing
- Process supplier invoices accurately and within agreed service levels.
- Validate invoice details and ensure compliance with company policies.
- Monitor invoice workflow queues and resolve processing exceptions.
- Match invoices to purchase orders and goods receipts where applicable.

Supplier & Stakeholder Support
- Respond to supplier and internal customer queries via email and telephone.
- Manage shared Accounts Payable mailboxes, ensuring prompt responses.
- Investigate and resolve invoice, payment, and account discrepancies.
- Build and maintain positive working relationships with suppliers and internal stakeholders.

Reconciliations & Financial Controls
- Assist with supplier statement reconciliations.
- Support month-end processes and reporting activities.
- Maintain accurate financial records and audit trails.
- Ensure compliance with internal controls, company policies, and audit requirements.

Administrative & Team Support
- Support data cleansing, reporting, and process improvement initiatives.
- Assist with Accounts Payable projects as required.
- Carry out general administrative tasks to support the wider finance team.

What We're Looking For
- Previous administrative experience, ideally within Finance or Accounts Payable.
- Excellent attention to detail with strong organisational skills.
- Strong communication and customer service skills.
- Ability to prioritise workloads and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, Outlook, and the wider Microsoft Office suite.
- Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively within a team.
- Experience using SAP, Ariba, VIM, or other ERP systems would be beneficial.

About You
We're looking for someone who is:

- A confident problem solver with a customer-focused approach.
- Adaptable and eager to learn new systems and processes.
- A supportive team player who enjoys working collaboratively.

What's in It for You?
- Gain valuable experience with one of the UK's leading FMCG organisations.
- Develop your Accounts Payable and finance administration skills.
- Gain exposure to SAP and Shared Services operations.
- Work within a collaborative, supportive, and professional team.
- Enhance your experience in a fast-paced finance environment with opportunities to broaden your knowledge.

If you're looking to build on your finance administration experience and want to join a supportive team where your contribution will make a real impact, we'd love to hear from you.

If you receive suspicious outreach claiming to be from us, please contact us via the ManpowerGroup website.

title: Finance Assistant
description:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for an enthusiastic and ambitious Finance Assistant to join a well-established organisation based in Solihull. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone at the early stages of their finance career who is looking to gain valuable experience, develop their accounting knowledge, and build a strong foundation within a supportive and forward-thinking business.

You may already have some experience within an administrative or finance environment or simply be looking for your first opportunity to develop a long-term career within Finance. The business is primarily looking for someone with a positive attitude, strong attention to detail, and a genuine willingness to learn. Working as part of a friendly and collaborative finance team, you will receive support and guidance from experienced professionals while gaining exposure to a range of day-to-day accounting processes. You will assist with the processing of purchase invoices, maintaining accurate financial records, allocating payments, and supporting with supplier and customer queries. As your knowledge and confidence grow, you will also have the opportunity to gain exposure to bank and account reconciliations.

Skills Required
- Some previous experience within an office, administration, customer service, or finance environment would be beneficial, although extensive finance experience is not essential.
- Strong attention to detail and a methodical approach to work, with the ability to handle information accurately and identify any discrepancies or errors.
- A genuine interest in building a long-term career within Finance and Accounting, with the ambition and motivation to continually develop your knowledge and skills.
- A proactive and positive attitude, with the confidence to ask questions, take ownership of tasks, and contribute positively to a collaborative team.

What You Will Receive
- Full training and ongoing support from experienced finance professionals who will help you build your technical knowledge, develop new skills, and grow in confidence.
- A varied role offering exposure to different areas of the finance function, allowing you to develop a broad understanding of transactional finance and wider accounting processes.
- Hybrid working opportunities, providing flexibility and helping you achieve a healthy work-life balance.
- The chance to work as part of a friendly, supportive, and collaborative team where you will be encouraged to ask questions, share ideas, and develop at your own pace.
- Long-term stability and the opportunity to build a genuine career within an organisation that recognises potential and actively supports internal progression.

Summary

This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to take their first step, or build on their existing experience, within Finance. Whether you have some previous administration or finance experience or are simply looking for a business that will give you the opportunity to learn and develop, this role offers an excellent platform to build a successful long-term career.

If you're ambitious, organised, numerically minded, and excited by the opportunity to develop within a supportive finance team, we'd love to hear from you.

description:
